observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

observation.setting: indoor stage with wooden flooring and black curtain backdrop, during a public performance
observation.dancers: group of women, approximately 8 dancers, plus a couple of people standing at the side operating microphones and playing flute/drum
observation.formation_and_space: starts with dancers entering from the sides, shifting between a curved line, pairs, and a horizontal line across the stage, traveling with skipping and stepping movements
observation.posture: upright torso with flexible upper body, slight knee flexion, and dynamic weight shifts
observation.footwork: energetic steps, skips, hops, and occasional crouching down or lunging on the beat; exact foot contact cannot be seen clearly due to costume length and camera distance
observation.arms_and_hands: arms raised above shoulder level or overhead, holding colorful scarves or handkerchiefs that are waved continuously
observation.hips_and_torso: gentle side-to-side torso sway and shoulder shrugs, reacting to arm and leg movements
observation.partnering: group formations with occasional hand-in-hand pairs or passing interactions, no close partner holds
observation.levels_jumps_turns: frequent level changes including crouching down low to the stage floor and rising back up, spins and turns performed individually and in pairs
observation.costume_and_props: traditional Punjabi women's attire consisting of bright salwar kameez suits in various colors (yellow, green, pink, blue), dupattas (scarves), and colorful handkerchiefs/scarves held in each hand
observation.cannot_infer: exact foot placement and rapid weight transfers are obscured by long kameez hems and low video resolution

signature_moments.what: dancers simultaneously crouch low towards the stage floor while waving scarves overhead, then rise back up
dancers hold arms overhead with hands extended upward and bounce on bent knees with lively footwork
pairs of dancers spin rapidly while holding colored scarves and traveling across the stage
